quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first arrives at the library - he cannot borrow a book until he walks through the door.
quests.explanation: Leo enters the library first, then browses the shelves, finds the book about rockets, and finally borrows it at the desk. The sequence moves logically from arrival to selection to borrowing - each step enabling the next.
sentences: Leo pushed open the heavy glass door of the local library.
He walked slowly along the shelves, reading each title carefully.
A book about rockets caught his eye and he pulled it from the shelf.
He carried it to the desk and borrowed it with his library card.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Leo first sits down at his desk - he cannot write his name before he is seated with paper in front of him.
quests.explanation: Leo sits down first, then takes out a pencil, writes his name at the top of the page, and decorates it. The sequence follows the natural preparation process before a writing task: sit, get your tool, write, then personalise.
sentences: Leo sat down at the wooden desk near the classroom window.
He took out his pencil and smoothed the sheet of paper flat.
He wrote his name at the very top of the page in large clear letters.
He drew a small star beside his name because he liked how it looked.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence that explains why the dog needs to visit the vet - the appointment cannot happen without a reason.
quests.explanation: The dog hurts its paw first, which is the reason for the vet visit. Leo carries the dog to the car, the vet examines the paw, and wraps it in a bandage. The story shows a clear problem-solution structure: injury, transport, diagnosis, treatment.
sentences: The dog hurt its front paw while running on the rocky path.
Leo carried the dog to the car and drove to the animal clinic.
The vet looked at the paw carefully under a bright light.
She wrapped the sore paw in a clean white bandage and smiled.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Identify the sentence where Mia first mixes the cake batter - baking cannot begin before the batter is ready.
quests.explanation: The batter is mixed first, then poured into a tin, baked in the oven, and removed when golden. This is a standard baking sequence: prepare mixture, pour into mould, apply heat, check and remove when done.
sentences: Mia mixed flour, eggs, butter, and sugar together in a large bowl.
She poured the smooth batter into a round tin lined with paper.
She put the tin in the oven and set the timer for thirty minutes.
She lifted out the golden cake and left it to cool on the rack.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first gets on his bike - he cannot start pedalling before he is seated and balanced.
quests.explanation: Leo gets on the bike first with his dad holding it steady, then tries to pedal, his dad lets go, and Leo rides on his own. The story shows a progression of growing independence: supported effort leads to unsupported success.
sentences: Leo climbed onto the small red bicycle and gripped the handlebars tightly.
His dad held the back of the seat to keep the bike steady.
Leo began to pedal slowly and tried to keep the front wheel straight.
His dad let go and Leo rode the full length of the path by himself.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where the children first arrive at the beach - the sandcastle cannot be built before they get there.
quests.explanation: The children arrive at the beach first, then collect wet sand, build the castle walls, and decorate it with shells. The story moves from arrival to gathering materials to building to the final creative touches.
sentences: The children ran down to the beach and dropped their bags on the dry sand.
They dug up handfuls of wet sand and packed it into a bucket.
They turned the bucket over and built four thick walls around the tower.
They pressed small shells into the walls to make windows and doors.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Mia first decides what to plant - she cannot prepare the soil before she knows what is going in it.
quests.explanation: Mia chooses her seeds first, then prepares the soil, plants the seeds in rows, and labels each row. This shows careful planning before physical action, demonstrating that good gardening begins with thought and preparation.
sentences: Mia chose packets of tomato and bean seeds from the garden shop.
She dug up the soil in the vegetable patch and broke up the hard clumps.
She made three shallow rows with a stick and dropped seeds into each one.
She pushed in small labels so she would remember what she had planted.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence that explains why Leo is in the kitchen - the purpose of being there must come before any action.
quests.explanation: Leo decides to make soup first, which brings him to the kitchen. He chops the vegetables, puts them in water to boil, and stirs them until tender. The story shows a logical cooking sequence where intent comes before the physical steps.
sentences: Leo decided to make vegetable soup for his family's lunch.
He washed and chopped two carrots, a potato, and an onion.
He put all the pieces into a large pot and covered them with water.
He stirred the pot gently until all the vegetables were soft and tender.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first picks up a bowl - a salad needs a container before the ingredients can be added.
quests.explanation: Leo gets the bowl first, then washes and tears the lettuce, adds cucumber and tomato, and finally drizzles on the dressing. The story follows a simple salad-making sequence where the container is prepared before the ingredients go in.
sentences: Leo took out a large wooden salad bowl from the kitchen cupboard.
He washed the lettuce leaves and tore them into bite-sized pieces.
He sliced cucumber and added cherry tomatoes to the bowl.
He drizzled olive oil and lemon juice over the top and tossed everything together.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence that explains why the dog needs a bath - the problem must come before the solution.
quests.explanation: The dog gets muddy first, which is the reason for the bath. Then Leo prepares the warm water, washes the dog, and dries it. The story has a clear cause-and-effect structure: a dirty dog causes a bathing event.
sentences: The dog ran through the muddy garden and got completely covered in dirt.
Leo filled the tub with warm water and added a drop of dog shampoo.
He lifted the dog in and scrubbed its fur from head to tail.
He lifted the dog out and wrapped it in a dry towel to rub it clean.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Mia first gets her art supplies ready - she cannot paint before she has her materials.
quests.explanation: Mia gathers her materials first, then sketches the outline, paints inside the lines, and waits for it to dry. The story follows a logical art process: prepare, sketch, paint, dry - each step depending on the previous one.
sentences: Mia set out her brushes, paints, and a large sheet of thick paper.
She drew the outline of a red house with a tall chimney in pencil first.
She dipped her brush in paint and carefully filled in each section with colour.
She put the painting on the windowsill and left it to dry in the sun.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Identify the sentence where Leo first notices the sprout - the plant must appear before he can react to it.
quests.explanation: The sprout appears first, then Leo waters it carefully, it grows taller each day, and eventually blooms into a full flower. The story shows the patient progress of growth, where early care leads to a final reward.
sentences: A tiny green sprout pushed up through the soil after one week.
Leo watered it gently each morning with a small yellow can.
The stem grew taller every day and two leaves opened wide.
By the end of the month, a bright yellow flower had fully opened.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Sam first spots the object on the beach - discovery must come before showing it to others.
quests.explanation: Sam spots the bottle on the beach first, then picks it up, notices there is a note inside, and pulls out the folded paper. The sequence builds curiosity: a discovery leads to investigation, which leads to finding something unexpected.
sentences: Sam was walking along the beach when he saw a glass bottle in the sand.
He picked it up and held it toward the sunlight to see inside.
He could see a small rolled piece of paper pushed deep into the neck.
He shook it out carefully and unfolded the damp, yellowed note.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Mia first sets her alarm - she cannot do her morning exercise before she wakes up on time.
quests.explanation: Mia sets her alarm first so she can wake up early enough for exercise. She gets up, goes outside, jogs around the block, and stretches when she returns. Early preparation (setting the alarm) makes the whole routine possible.
sentences: Mia set her alarm for half past six the night before.
When it rang, she got up straight away and put on her trainers.
She jogged around the block twice in the cool morning air.
She came back inside, stretched her legs, and made herself a warm drink.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first heats the milk - you need warm milk before you can make hot chocolate.
quests.explanation: The milk is heated first, then the cocoa powder is stirred in, the mixture is whisked until frothy, and poured into a mug. The story shows a simple but logical cooking sequence where heat is applied before mixing and serving.
sentences: Leo poured a cup of milk into a small saucepan and warmed it on the stove.
He added two teaspoons of dark cocoa powder and a pinch of sugar.
He whisked everything together until the top was covered in tiny bubbles.
He poured the hot chocolate into a wide mug and added two marshmallows.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Mia first stands at the edge of the pool - she cannot enter the water before she is at the pool.
quests.explanation: Mia stands at the pool edge first, then lowers herself in with her teacher nearby, kicks across the shallow end, and reaches the other side. The sequence shows a beginner swimmer gaining confidence: starting at the edge, entering cautiously, attempting the skill, and succeeding.
sentences: Mia stood at the edge of the shallow end and looked at the blue water.
She lowered herself in slowly while her teacher stood beside her.
She took a breath, pushed off the wall, and kicked her feet hard.
She reached the other side and held on to the rail with a big smile.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Leo first tips out the blocks - building cannot begin before the materials are out.
quests.explanation: Leo tips out the blocks first, then sorts them by size, starts stacking them from largest to smallest, and places the final block on top to complete the tower. The story shows a methodical building process where planning and sorting lead to a stable structure.
sentences: Leo tipped the whole box of wooden blocks onto the carpet.
He sorted them into three groups by size: big, medium, and small.
He began stacking the largest pieces at the bottom to keep it steady.
He placed the last tiny block on the very top and stepped back to look.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where the family first arrives at the park - the picnic cannot begin before they reach the spot.
quests.explanation: The family arrives at the park first, spreads the blanket on the grass, unpacks the food, and eats lunch together. The sequence shows the preparation and enjoyment of an outdoor meal, where location and setup must come before the meal itself.
sentences: The family drove to the park and parked the car near the old oak tree.
They spread a large chequered blanket on the flat grass by the pond.
Mia opened the basket and laid out sandwiches, fruit, and cold juice.
They ate their lunch on the grass and watched the ducks swim past.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo's mum first writes the shopping list - you need a list before you can shop for specific items.
quests.explanation: The list is written first, which guides all the shopping that follows. Leo and his mum go to the market, buy items from the list, and pay at the end. The story shows how preparation (writing a list) leads to an organised and efficient shopping trip.
sentences: Leo's mum wrote a list of six things they needed from the market.
She and Leo walked through the busy stalls looking for each item.
They picked up tomatoes, onions, bread, and a pot of local honey.
They paid for everything at the last stall and carried the bags to the car.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Mia first holds the scissors - she cannot cut anything before she picks them up.
quests.explanation: Mia picks up the scissors first, then practises opening and closing them, tries cutting along a straight line, and finally cuts out a shape successfully. The story shows a learning process: tool handling leads to practice, which leads to successful use.
sentences: Mia picked up the round-tipped scissors and held them the right way.
She practised opening and closing the blades a few times slowly.
She placed them at the edge of the paper and cut along a straight line.
She cut out a neat square on her first try and held it up proudly.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first folds the paper into a triangular shape - that first fold creates the hull of the boat.
quests.explanation: The first fold creates the basic shape that all other folds build on. Leo folds the paper into a triangle, folds up the edges, shapes the opening, and places the boat in water to test it. The story follows a craft process where each fold is essential to the next.
sentences: Leo folded a square sheet of paper in half to make a triangle.
He folded the two bottom corners up to make a wide, flat rim.
He pulled the two sides apart gently to open the bottom of the boat.
He placed it in a bowl of water and watched it float without sinking.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Leo first switches the computer on - nothing else can happen until the machine is running.
quests.explanation: Leo switches the computer on first, then waits for it to load, opens the typing programme, and begins the lesson. The sequence shows the logical steps of starting a technology session: power on, wait, open the correct programme, then learn.
sentences: Leo pressed the power button and the computer screen lit up slowly.
He waited for the machine to load and then clicked on the icon.
He opened the typing programme and saw the colourful keyboard on screen.
He practised typing his name and the names of all his family members.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first sits in the barber's chair - the haircut cannot begin before he is seated.
quests.explanation: Leo sits in the chair first, then the barber capes him to protect his clothes, cuts his hair, and shows him the result with a mirror. This follows the real-world sequence of a haircut from sitting down to the final reveal.
sentences: Leo climbed up into the tall barber's chair and put his feet on the rest.
The barber clipped a striped cape around Leo's neck to catch the hair.
He combed Leo's hair flat and began to cut neatly around the sides.
He held a small mirror behind Leo's head to show the finished cut.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Leo first gathers the materials for his kite - building cannot begin before the supplies are collected.
quests.explanation: The materials are gathered first, then Leo follows the instructions to assemble the frame, stretches the fabric over it, and adds the tail and string. The story shows a construction project that requires careful preparation before the building steps begin.
sentences: Leo collected two thin sticks, a sheet of orange plastic, and a ball of string.
He followed the picture in the book and tied the sticks into a cross shape.
He stretched the orange plastic over the frame and taped down each edge.
He tied a long tail of ribbons at the bottom and attached the flying string.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first arrives at the dentist - the examination cannot begin before he is in the right place.
quests.explanation: Leo arrives at the dentist first, then waits and is called in, opens his mouth for the examination, and leaves with a new toothbrush. The story shows the complete sequence of a dental visit, from arrival to departure.
sentences: Leo arrived at the dentist with his mum and signed in at the front desk.
He sat in the waiting room until the nurse called his name.
He opened his mouth wide while the dentist counted all his teeth.
The dentist said everything looked great and gave him a new blue toothbrush.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Mia first sits down at the art table - the drawing lesson cannot begin before she is in her seat with materials ready.
quests.explanation: Mia sits down and arranges her materials first, then the teacher demonstrates the technique, Mia copies it carefully, and the teacher praises the result. The story shows a learning sequence: setup, instruction, imitation, feedback.
sentences: Mia sat at the art table and laid out her pencils in a neat row.
The teacher showed the class how to draw a bowl of fruit with curved lines.
Mia copied each shape carefully, starting with the wide round bowl.
The teacher walked past, looked at her work, and said it was very good.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where the class first enters the museum - the paintings on the wall cannot be seen before they go inside.
quests.explanation: The class enters the museum first, then is guided to the main gallery, the teacher explains each painting, and finally the students sketch their favourite one. The story shows the stages of a museum visit: arrive, navigate, learn, respond creatively.
sentences: The class arrived at the art museum and walked through the tall entrance doors.
A guide led them down a wide corridor to the main gallery on the second floor.
The teacher stopped at each painting and explained what made it special.
The students sat on the floor and sketched their favourite painting on the wall.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where the school sports day first starts - the races cannot happen before the event begins.
quests.explanation: The sports day begins with the announcement first, then the first race is run, Leo's team wins the relay, and the day ends with a medal ceremony. The story moves through the chronological stages of a sports day event.
sentences: The teacher blew a whistle and announced the start of the school sports day.
The first race was a sprint across the field between the four houses.
Leo ran the last leg of the relay and crossed the finish line ahead of everyone.
The headteacher gave out medals at the end while parents clapped from the side.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Look for the sentence where Leo first opens his school bag - he cannot pack it before he checks what is already inside.
quests.explanation: Leo opens the bag first to check what is there, then gets out his list, adds the missing items, and zips it up ready for the morning. The story shows the value of checking and planning before completing a task.
sentences: Leo opened his school bag and tipped everything out onto his bed.
He found his reading list and checked each item one by one.
He added his maths book and his swimming kit from the bottom drawer.
He zipped his bag shut and left it by the front door for the morning.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.

quests.hint: Find the sentence where Leo first comes home from school - the snack preparation cannot begin before he arrives.
quests.explanation: Leo comes home first, drops his bag, and then goes to the kitchen. He toasts the bread, spreads peanut butter on it, and eats it at the table. The story shows a simple after-school routine where arriving home enables all the actions that follow.
sentences: Leo came home from school and dropped his bag in the hallway.
He went to the kitchen and put two slices of bread in the toaster.
When the toast popped up, he spread peanut butter thick on each slice.
He sat at the kitchen table and ate his snack before starting his homework.
quests.instruction: Read the sentences and arrange them in the correct order.
